Walked through streaming behavior, key request params (max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop tokens), retry/backoff and idempotency considerations, and a short Console tour for per-route latency/cost. transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-09 15:00 UTC — duration 47m. Attendees listed above.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone — thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. We've got Priya, our SE, and Sam who will jump in with the console demo. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Lena: Good thanks, Jordan. Excited — we just want a short hands-on of the hosted API for chat gen, mainly streaming, params and what to do when things error out.
[00:18] Jordan: Perfect that's exactly what we'll show. Priya, you want to intro the lab?
[00:21] Priya: Yeah hi all — real quick plan: 10 minutes on core streaming behavior and request params, 15 minutes live sandbox runs (I'll paste curl and SDK calls), then 15 on retry/backoff, idempotency and Console/Optimize tips and finally Q&A. Sound ok?
[00:33] Marco: Sounds great. We're especially worried about tail latency and cost per token.
[00:37] Priya: Totally. We'll show the console traces so you can see token breakdown and how batching/kv cache affects unit cost.
[00:45] Jordan: One quick administrative note — are there any security or compliance blockers up front? SAML / SSO, SOC2?
[00:50] Aisha: We need SOC2 certificate and we use SAML SSO internally. Also KMS for keys ideally.
[00:55] Jordan: Great — we will share security pack after the call. Redwood supports SSO and KMS/HSM integrations and SOC2. I'll follow up with the docs.

[05:00] Priya: Ok, starting the demo — this is the hosted chat endpoint in the sandbox. First behavior: streaming. When you open a stream you'll get incremental partial chunks — useful for UI latency. Note partials are not final predictions; in speech it's like interim captions.
[05:20] Jordan: One common gotcha — streaming shows partial tokens and can be restarted on retries; your frontend should handle deduping partials vs final.
[05:35] Kenji: If we reconnect and resume, does the service replay the entire context or just deltas?
[05:40] Priya: We replay deltas where possible, but to be safe you should send a conversation snapshot up to the last confirmed user message. We also support KV cache reuse if you're pinning model variants. Some transcriptions will show "K V cache" spelled out in places.

[10:00] Priya: Live curl example: POST to /v1/chat with messages array, set stream=true for SSE. Key params: max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop tokens. We'll paste this in chat.
[10:20] (Priya pastes curl)
[10:30] Marco: Quick question — which param most affects hallucinations?
[10:33] Priya: Temperature and top_p. Lower temperature reduces randomness; top_p controls nucleus sampling. Also good prompt engineering and stop tokens cut off generation where applicable. For deterministic outputs set temperature ~0 and top_p ~0.0-0.1.

[15:00] Priya: Now a small failure mode — we purposely induced a partial drop mid-stream. Watch how the stream emits a 5xx and then our SDK triggers exponential backoff.
[15:18] Sam: The SDK includes automatic retry for idempotent requests. For non-idempotent generation (streams that have side effects) we recommend client-controlled retries with idempotency keys. We usually attach a client_message_id to each user turn.
[15:40] Aisha: So idempotency key is our responsibility?
[15:42] Priya: Yes — you supply an idempotency_key header. For simple text generation where you can tolerate duplicates, the SDK retry policy is fine; for billing and dedupe we recommend explicit keys.

[20:00] Priya: Backoff: use jittered exponential backoff. Example: base 500ms, multiplier 2x, max 8s, with full jitter. Avoid tight retry loops because they inflate load and cost.
[20:20] Kenji: Any rate limit headers we can read to adaptively backoff?
[20:24] Priya: Yes the API returns x-rate-limit-remaining and a Retry-After when throttled. Console traces also show per-route QPS metrics.

[25:00] Priya: Now let's look at the Console — Sam, can you show the token breakdown?
[25:10] Sam: Sure. Here is a sample route — per-token cost, P95 latency and token counts. The Console groups by model variant so you can see the cost impact if you switch to a quantized variant.
[25:30] Sam: Also we surface prefix cache hits — which we call KV cache reuse — that reduces model work when you've repeated prompts or system instructions.
[25:45] Marco: If we use dedicated capacity versus hosted, how different are the SLOs?
[25:50] Jordan: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and private pools with higher SLAs, hosted is multi-tenant but we still publish performance profiles. For strict latency SLOs we recommend Dedicated or pinning to a lower-latency model variant.

[30:00] Priya: Optimize suggestions: 1) batch short messages to amortize GPU overhead, 2) enable prefix KV caching for repeated system messages, 3) use a quantized variant (8-bit or 4-bit) if high throughput with slightly lower quality is acceptable, 4) tune max_tokens per user turn to the minimum needed.
[30:25] Lena: For batching — how does that affect user perceived latency?
[30:28] Priya: Batching is tradeoff — it improves throughput and lowers cost per token but you increase queuing latency. We recommend adaptive batching: small immediate responses for interactive UI, larger batches for background tasks (summaries).

[35:00] Priya: Quick note on safety: if you use stop tokens, model guarentees for truncation are best-effort. Also we recommend server-side safety filters or a secondary reranker to catch edge cases.

[36:00] Marco: For retries, do we get chargedback for partially generated tokens that then fail?
[36:05] Jordan: You get billed for tokens processed by the model. If a stream fails mid-generation you are charged for tokens consumed. That's why idempotency + conservative retry logic matters. We'll include guidance in the follow-up doc.

[40:00] Priya: Wrapping up — we pushed a small guided exercise: run the sandbox curl we pasted, try toggling temperature and stream=true/false, trigger an intentional error and observe console traces.
[40:15] Lena: We'll run that and get back to you.
[40:20] Aisha: And we'll need the SOC2 and SAML docs.
[40:25] Jordan: Yep I'll send the security pack. Priya will share the Optimize spreadsheet and sample SDK snippets.

[45:00] Jordan: Any other questions?
[45:05] Kenji: One last — can Redwood run a short perf benchmark with our typical token mix?
[45:10] Jordan: Yes we can — that would be a scoped POC. We'll propose a runbook after your smoke test.
[46:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and snippets.

End transcript.

Notes: occasional transcript artifacts e.g., misheard acronyms ("K V cache" spelled occasionally), filler words and overlapping talk. References shared: sandbox curl (link sent in chat), console screenshot (link), security pack (link to drive).
